Before you get started. Three rules:

-YOU NEVER DIVE ALONE

-YOU NEVER DIVE ALONE

-YOUR KNIFE IS NOW PART OF YOUR BODY

You may have noticed that YOU NEVER DIVE ALONE is up there twice.

That's because YOU NEVER DIVE ALONE.

You shallow water blackout, you get tangled, a fin gets stuck and you don't have a buddy? You die. Simple as that. No redo's, No second chances, you'll be missing, and they may never find you. If you have a couple of frisky sharks, you don't have a buddy, you are now in danger, as sharks will work the angles and you can only keep eyes in one direction at a time.

You never dive without your knife. Your knife is as essential as your arm from now on. If you get tangled, if a fin gets stuck, you cut it off to free yourself. If you don't have a knife, you die. Do not pass go, do not go home. You get the idea. That said, if you lose your knife (which you probably will eventually) don't cry. Call it a day if you don't have a backup or get another one. You can minimize the risk by having a backup and attaching both via coiled plastic kind of like telephone cord. It allows maneuverability, while keeping it attached.

You'll also need this to "brain" or kill fish if your shot doesn't stonewall them right away. A struggling fish is not only unethical, but it scares other fish, attracts predators and can be dangerous since there is a sharp spear attached to it that is now flailing about.

If a shark approaches you and your dive buddy aggressively, remain calm - prey flinches. Keep eyes on the shark at all times and keep it at spear's length and give it a poke if it gets too frisky. That said, don't try to engage a shark if it isn't necessary. They are better than you in the water, but are mostly opportunistic hunters. If they (one or more) start to frenzy, keep eyes on and calmly swim away and try to get out of the water. Relocate far away or call it a day. All it takes is a bite out in the ocean and two things will happen - you'll bleed which can be life threatening if serious enough. And the blood will attract more predators. It's not worth it.

If for some reason all of this fails and you get attacked, go for the eyes or snout with your fists, your knife, your spear or whatever is handy. Secondary target is the gills. Don't end up here.
